oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and states they can be used interchangeably.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token claims as token confusion; use access_token as the API bearer credential in tests.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the granted scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing profile/email/phone/address fields without corresponding scopes is expected, not claim stripping.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and allows them to contain the same claims.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token claim sets as overbroad authorization by themselves; this is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Session-based authentication using cookies grants full MCP tool access without scope filtering, while Bearer tokens enforce scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Use Bearer tokens for scope tests; cookie-auth full access is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to admins and global admins.
oidc_jwt.note: Admin accounts are unsuitable negative controls for tag-based authorization tests.

oidc_jwt.description: Using authorization_code grant with code='guest-user' creates a temporary guest account instead of completing a normal code flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Guest usernames are auto-generated as guest_<uuid>; this is a product feature, not an identity mix-up.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges under configured auto-linking are by design and should not be flagged as cross-user collision.

oidc_jwt.description: For Lark OAuth, Casdoor derives username from UserId, then UnionId, then OpenId.
oidc_jwt.note: Granted identity may reflect provider-specific fallback identifiers rather than a human-readable username.

oidc_jwt.description: For Baidu OAuth, Casdoor uses Baidu's masked username value as the username.
oidc_jwt.note: A masked or transformed username from the provider is expected and should not be treated as normalization confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Submitting code=guest-user to the authorization_code token endpoint creates a guest user with username guest_<uuid> and tag guest-user.
oidc_jwt.note: This special code path is a documented extension and should not be treated as unauthorized code acceptance.

oidc_jwt.description: When exclusive sign-in is enabled on an application, a new login removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
oidc_jwt.note: Loss of prior session after a second login is expected behavior, not session fixation or revocation bug.

oidc_jwt.description: SSO logout invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and introspection/refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token rejection is expected and should be used as the oracle for logout tests.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor documentation describes JWT access tokens as bearer tokens and does not document jti replay tracking for normal JWT bearer use.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same JWT bearer token is not by itself evidence of an anti-replay failure for stateless JWT validation.

oidc_jwt.description: Admins can create or change providers, applications, redirect URIs, and related trust settings; new logins using the updated configuration are expected to follow the new trust anchor or client configuration.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful login after an admin intentionally changed provider/application trust settings. Only flag if old configuration remains accepted unexpectedly after the change.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and treats them as interchangeable.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical claims or same-token behavior between access_token and id_token as token confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims covered by the granted scope; with openid alone it may return only sub, iss, and aud.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing email/profile fields without corresponding scopes is expected, not claim stripping.

oidc_jwt.description: Shared applications are referenced with an organization-specific -org-<organizationName> suffix in client_id or application name.
oidc_jwt.note: Organization-specific client identifiers are expected and should not be treated as audience rewriting bugs.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and normal authorization_code tests, the redirect_uri used at /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token MUST match exactly. Casdoor documentation explicitly states the resource parameter must match exactly across authorize and token requests, and OAuth callback handling assumes the same redirect URI; mismatches will fail by design rather than indicate a flow-coherence bug.

For I5 audience-binding tests using RFC 8707 resource indicators, include the same resource value in BOTH start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token. Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI only when resource is supplied, and the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests. If omitted or mismatched, audience results are not meaningful.

For I3 PKCE tests, when code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 are sent at authorization time, exchange_code_for_token MUST include the original code_verifier. Casdoor supports PKCE and states that with PKCE enabled client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must still be correct. Do not interpret failures from wrong client_secret as PKCE enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token style freshness tests against Casdoor-issued tokens, include a CONTROL flow that obtains a valid token from the same application and verifies it via /api/userinfo or /api/login/oauth/introspect. Without a control, a failed attack flow may be caused by bad client_id, redirect_uri, or application grant-type configuration rather than time validation.

Refresh token expiration has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Documentation does not describe 0 as literal immediate expiry; it is the platform default setting value. Never assume 0 means 'already expired' in tests. Configure a positive refresh lifetime explicitly when refresh behavior matters.

Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout set to 0 means use the global default, not literal zero-second resend. Do not use 0 when testing timing or rate-limit behavior; set an explicit positive value if resend timing matters.

Cookie/session expiration has a numeric sentinel: CookieExpireInHours of 0 means use the default (720 hours), not immediate expiry. Do not use 0 in session-freshness tests expecting instant invalidation.

For I2 replay_same_token on JWT bearer tokens, do NOT flag reuse of the same Casdoor access token as a vulnerability by itself. Casdoor issues bearer JWTs and the docs describe standard OAuth token use plus introspection/logout invalidation; stateless bearer reuse is by design unless a specific one-time semantic is documented.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request a narrower scope explicitly in token_exchange and compare the returned scope/claims against the original token. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, so omitting scope cannot test downscoping or escalation behavior.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the resource parameter during the original authorization flow so the subject token aud is bound to a service URI. Without resource, the access token audience defaults to the client_id, which changes the meaning of audience-binding results.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to granted scope only. For I4/I5 verification, request the needed scopes during login; otherwise missing email/profile/phone/address fields in verify_granted_identity are by design and must not be treated as dropped claims or authorization bugs.

Casdoor states access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably. This is by design. Tests must still treat access_token as the session credential for API calls, but should not flag identical payloads between access_token and id_token as a token-confusion vulnerability.

For I5 claim-shape tests involving address, token format matters. Only JWT-Standard yields an OIDC-compliant address object; JWT, JWT-Empty, and JWT-Custom return address as a raw string array. Do not flag non-object address in non-Standard formats as a bug.

For I4 case-confusion tests, organization setting isUsernameLowered controls whether usernames are converted to lowercase. If enabled, case folding is by design and 'Admin' vs 'admin' may intentionally collapse. Record the setting before interpreting collisions.

For I4 username/email binding tests, organization setting 'Use email as username' causes the email to become the username when the username field is hidden, and changing email updates username to match. Do not treat username=email derivation as an identity-collision bug.

For multi-tenant tests, shared applications intentionally use organization-qualified client identifiers by appending '-org-<organizationName>' to the base client_id or application name. Cross-org differences in client_id under shared applications are by design and must be preserved in test setup.

For OIDC/OAuth client registration tests, discover the registration endpoint from /.well-known/openid-configuration and use /api/oauth/register only if DCR is enabled for the organization. If dcrPolicy is disabled, registration failures are expected and not security findings.

DCR requires at least one redirect_uris entry. Registration failures without redirect_uris are setup errors, not authorization failures. Applications created through DCR also receive defaults such as authorization_code grant and 7-day token expiration unless overridden.

For OIDC callback tests against desktop/MCP clients using localhost callbacks, Casdoor examples rely on wildcard localhost redirect URIs such as http://127.0.0.1:*/callback and http://localhost:*/callback. Exact redirect URI matching still applies at runtime; ensure the actual callback URI is pre-registered in the application according to the platform's wildcard support.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and general authorization-code tests, the redirect_uri used at /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token MUST match exactly. Casdoor documentation explicitly states the resource indicator must match exactly between authorization and token requests, and OAuth callback handling depends on the configured Redirect URL. Do not vary redirect_uri between steps unless intentionally testing mismatch rejection.

For RFC 8707 audience/resource tests, if start_oidc_auth includes resource, exchange_code_for_token MUST include the identical resource value. Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI and requires the resource to match exactly between authorization and token requests. A mismatch causes setup failure rather than an authorization-binding finding.

For I2 expired_token and future_token style tests against Casdoor-issued tokens, include a CONTROL flow that obtains a valid token from the same application and verifies it via /api/userinfo or /api/login/oauth/introspect. Without a control, a failed attack flow may be caused by bad client_id, redirect_uri, disabled grant type, or missing provider/application setup rather than token freshness enforcement.

Casdoor supports PKCE on the authorization code flow. When testing PKCE-related I3/OIDC flow coherence, start_oidc_auth MUST send code_challenge_method=S256 and code_challenge, and exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct. Do not interpret success without PKCE as a vulnerability unless the application was explicitly configured to require PKCE.

For token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documentation states that omitting scope causes the new token to inherit the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing to a subset. The fuzzer MUST compare requested exchanged scope against the original subject token scope and treat broader requested scopes as the attack case; inherited same-scope behavior is by design.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the token endpoint /api/login/oauth/access_token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and map the target audience to the documented resource parameter when testing service binding. Casdoor documentation describes resource as the service-binding input that drives the aud claim; failing to set it yields ambiguous audience results.

Casdoor access_token and id_token are documented as identical in payload and usable interchangeably, but session_token for subsequent API calls MUST still be mapped to access_token, not id_token. The fuzzer should not flag identical payloads between access_token and id_token as an I5 bug; this is documented behavior.

Refresh token lifetime has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Documentation states 'default 0 hours' for refresh token expiration. Treat value 0 as a special configuration meaning the application default/current configured refresh-token lifetime behavior, not as evidence of an immediately expired access token. Do not hardcode assumptions about zero meaning disabled without confirming application settings.

Verification code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout set to 0 means use the global default, not literal zero-second resend. Do not build timing assertions that assume 0 disables throttling; 0 selects inherited default behavior.

For multi-tenant tests, organizations are first-class security boundaries in Casdoor. User identifiers are commonly represented as <organization>/<username>, and shared applications append -org-<organizationName> to client_id or application name. The fuzzer MUST keep organization context explicit when comparing identities or audiences; cross-org acceptance may be caused by intentionally shared applications rather than identity collapse.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor can be configured with isUsernameLowered at the server level and also supports case-insensitive automatic account linking by username for OAuth providers. The fuzzer MUST record whether username lowering or auto-linking is enabled before treating case folding as a collision bug.

For I4 multi-identity tests involving external OAuth/OIDC providers, Casdoor supports automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone, or username (case-insensitive). If linking is enabled, two upstream identities may intentionally merge into one Casdoor user. The fuzzer MUST disable or account for auto-linking before flagging identity merge as a principal-binding violation.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests against MCP or other scoped APIs, session-based authentication via browser cookies bypasses scope checking and grants full access by design. The fuzzer MUST use Bearer access tokens, not session cookies, when testing whether granted permissions exceed requested scopes.

For OIDC userinfo verification, Casdoor returns claims according to the granted scope. Missing profile/email/address/phone fields in /api/userinfo are not authorization bugs if those scopes were not requested during token issuance. The fuzzer MUST request the relevant scopes in start_oidc_auth or token requests before asserting missing or extra claims.

For DCR-based tests, Dynamic Client Registration is controlled per organization by dcrPolicy and may be disabled. A failed registration when DCR is disabled is expected setup behavior, not a protocol-security finding. Also, DCR requires at least one redirect_uri.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and PKCE-bound authorization-code tests, start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token MUST use the exact same redirect_uri unless the test intentionally targets mismatch handling. Casdoor documentation explicitly requires the provider callback to return to the same redirect_uri and examples show the token exchange using the same redirect_uri value.

For I5 audience-binding tests using RFC 8707 resource indicators, if start_oidc_auth includes resource then exchange_code_for_token MUST include the same resource value exactly. Casdoor states the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests; otherwise failures are setup errors, not security findings.

For I2 future_token/expired_token control planning, access token lifetime is application-configured via ExpireInHours and token endpoint returns expires_in. Refresh token lifetime is separately configured via RefreshExpireInHours. Do not hardcode expected lifetimes; read expires_in from the response or configure the application explicitly.
Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables resend delay or means immediate resend.

Numeric sentinel: refresh token expiration default is 0 hours unless configured on the application. Documentation does not define 0 as 'never expires'; treat 0 as platform-specific default/disabled refresh behavior and configure RefreshExpireInHours explicitly for tests that require refresh or long-lived sessions.

For I2 token-freshness tests (expired_token, future_token, nbf), include a CONTROL flow using a valid token from the same application and client configuration. Without a control, a failed attack login may be caused by disabled grant types, wrong redirect_uri, wrong client credentials, or application misconfiguration rather than time validation.

For I1/I5 token_exchange tests, Casdoor supports subject_token_type values access_token, jwt, and id_token. The fuzzer MUST set subject_token_type explicitly to match the token being exchanged; otherwise a rejection may be due to token-type mismatch rather than audience/scope enforcement.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documentation says omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, while provided scope is intended to narrow permissions. Therefore the fuzzer MUST compare requested exchanged scope against the original subject token scope and treat broader requested scopes as attack inputs; a successful exchange that returns broader claims than the original authorization indicates a real issue.

For I1/I5 cross-provider audience tests, when using resource indicators Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI instead of the client_id. The oracle MUST validate audience against the configured resource when resource was requested, not against client_id.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo response is scope-dependent. verify_granted_identity may return only sub/iss/aud for scope=openid. Missing email/profile fields are not evidence of stripping or authorization bugs unless those scopes were requested during token issuance.

Casdoor states access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably by design. Do NOT flag identical claims across access_token and id_token as a token-confusion vulnerability; this is documented platform behavior.

For I2 replay_same_token on ordinary JWT bearer access tokens, do NOT treat reuse of the same access token as a vulnerability by itself. Casdoor documents stateless JWT-style token use and does not claim jti replay tracking for bearer tokens.

For I3 config-change sequences involving trust or application settings, admin changes are expected to take effect for NEW logins. Only flag a coherence issue if old behavior persists unexpectedly after the configuration change, not merely because a new login follows the updated configuration.

For OIDC authorization-code tests with PKCE, when code_challenge was sent in start_oidc_auth, exchange_code_for_token SHOULD include the matching code_verifier. If omitted, failure is expected and should be interpreted as flow rejection, not identity mismatch. Casdoor also states client_secret becomes optional with PKCE, but if provided it must be correct.

For OIDC request-object or nonce-related tests, the provided Casdoor docs do not document support for request JWT parameters or nonce validation behavior on /login/oauth/authorize. Do not infer undocumented request-object validation semantics from generic OIDC expectations when classifying failures.

For multi-tenant/shared-application tests, shared applications require the client_id or application name to be suffixed with -org-<organizationName>. Using the unsuffixed client_id against another organization is invalid setup, not evidence of cross-tenant acceptance.

For multi-tenant setup, only the built-in organization can create shared applications. Tests that rely on shared-application cross-org behavior must provision the application under built-in first; creating it elsewhere will not model the documented feature correctly.

For I4 case-confusion tests, organization setting isUsernameLowered can force usernames to lowercase. If enabled, case-folding collisions may be by configuration rather than a broker bug; record the setting before interpreting Admin vs admin results.

For I4 identity-binding tests involving external OAuth/OIDC providers, Casdoor can automatically link accounts by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. Cross-login merges under those configured linking rules are by design and must not be flagged as unintended principal collapse without ruling out configured auto-linking.

For I4 username derivation tests on specific providers, Casdoor may derive the local username from provider-specific identifiers rather than a JWT/OIDC preferred_username claim. Documented examples include Lark preferring UserId then UnionId then OpenId, DingTalk using unionid, and Baidu using a masked username. These derivations are by design.
For I5 application-tag authorization tests, admins and global admins bypass application tag restrictions by design. Do not use admin accounts as negative controls for tag-based denial tests.

For I5 guest-user tests, code='guest-user' on the authorization_code token exchange is a Casdoor extension that intentionally creates a temporary user with username guest_<uuid> and tag guest-user. This is not an authorization bypass; tests must distinguish guest creation from normal code exchange.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
